prompt:
Generate one high-quality cinematic 16:9 image for the specified section, not a generic slide or dashboard. No letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, arrows, diagrams, interface, checkmarks, traffic-light statuses or readable documents. The compositor adds every semantic mark independently. Do not invent a completed publication, a live security test, a solved outing, approval or consensus. Fictional editorial staging, not documentary evidence. Rich material detail, carefully controlled light, credible objects and hands. Keep designated annotation zones visually quiet. Never fill quiet zones with invented panels. Reference images establish cast and room identity only; follow this section's camera and blocking.
VISUAL FORMAT: human-time-conflict
TEACHING PURPOSE: Put two people's travel constraint against a successful booking immediately.
CAMERA: Eye-level human scene with a long horizontal travel horizon.
The same fictional silver-haired woman in an olive jacket and close-cropped man in a sand sweater stand together at a quiet covered bus shelter in late-afternoon blue light. They are concerned and thinking, not stranded or celebrating. No bus departure is depicted. A softly lit community room is visible far across the street, with no crowd or event. Place the TWO people in the RIGHT THIRD; LEFT TWO THIRDS contain quiet blue shelter glass and open sky for a booking artifact and qualitative time conflict. No timetable, clocks, route maps, writing, ticket numbers or signage. Fictional staging of a reported concern, not a claim that they traveled or missed a bus.
COMPOSITING INTENT: A small confirmed booking ticket contrasts with a long last-bus-before-event-end axis. The two affected people stay visibly present at the far end of the composition.
SEMANTIC AUTHORITY FOR CONTEXT ONLY, NEVER RENDER THESE WORDS: FICTIONAL ENGINEERING VARIANT. The booking tool succeeds. Reservation R seventeen exists. The agent reports: outing arranged. But two members cannot attend: their last bus leaves before the event ends. Moving the event could disrupt other members who already planned around it. Booked, but still stuck.
